title: Albums Of The Week: Remote Viewing | State Violence

content:
THE EDITED PRESS RELEASE: “The crushing new album from London heavyweights Remote Viewing, State Violence is their most direct statement — an unapologetic reflection on the increasing levels of injustice, social division, extreme wealth and human atrocities we are seeing the world over. Across seven tracks, Remote Viewing sharpen their explosive confrontational sound that resides between gritty sludge-metal riffs and the ear-splitting power of noise-rock.

Remote Viewing formed from the ashes of Palehorse, consisting of members of Million Dead, Sly & The Family Drone and Hands Up Who Wants To Die. To capture State Violence, the quintet returned to Bear Bites Horse Studio in their hometown to work with long-time collaborator — producer, engineer and Petbrick musician Wayne Adams (who has helmed acclaimed heavy records by Green Lung, USA Nails, Vacuous, Kulk and countless more) with Stephen Kerrison adding his mastering magic touch. The album also features an array of special guests, including Hannah Asprey of Ian and Ross Sargeant of Pascagoula on track Human Right$, adding a rare glimpse of beauty and melodicism within an album of ugliness and horror.

Studying Remote Viewing’s song titles and lyrics has always revealed a love for absurd self-deprecating humour and personal in-jokes, but the band are in less of a laughing mood on State Violence. “We’re aware of the state of the world around us and not everything is funny right now,” laments guitarist James Bryant. “Many still believe the atrocities they see on their phone screens occur only in faraway places, maintaining an ‘it couldn’t happen here’ mentality, when injustice and corruption are already occurring at home, not just abroad.” Atkins sums it up even more bluntly, “The world is currently a veritable shit show of epic proportions.”

Remote Viewing have become both revered and feared for their loud and confrontational live shows, feeling at home on the smaller stages where no barriers separate performers from their audience. Never a band to be boxed into one scene, they favour diverse bills. “We’re too weird for the doom/sludge scene, and too heavy for the art-rock scene,” suggests Bryant, “we just exist caught somewhere between those worlds.” Remote Viewing have shared stages with Thou, Moloch, Future Of The Left, Sugar Horse, Wren, Great Falls, Dawn Ray’d and countless others. In 2024, Remote Viewing embarked on a tour with like-minded peers Pascagoula. The noisy quintet have appeared at Desertfest London, Chimpy Fest and Dreadfest, and will continue to march forth and bust eardrums to come.”
